title: Tradeoff notice and replay consent template — customer-facing
content:
Purpose (what this draft is):
A concise, customer-focused template to announce: 1) the tradeoffs we made during an incident (why we temporarily favored availability/latency over strict response integrity), and 2) an opt-in replay/verification path so tenants can request replays of affected inference requests and consent to outcome reconciliation.

Quick context (internal note):
- Use when incident remediation required aggressive routing or fallback to approximate model variants, KV-cache bypasses, or prefix-trimming that may have resulted in degraded output fidelity for a bounded window.
- Avoid heavyweight legal language here; this is operational/technical + choices for product teams.
- Keep the top section short for status pages; expand in a follow-up postmortem for customers.

Sample short status page update (reduce to ~2–3 sentences):
Redwood is investigating an incident affecting inference fidelity for a subset of requests in us-west-2 between 2029-05-29 03:12–03:47 UTC. We temporarily routed traffic to a lower-capacity fallback model and applied prefix-preserving cache-bypass to preserve latency SLOs; some responses may be incomplete or less precise. If you suspect impacted requests, see the replay and verification options below or contact cs@redwood.ai for immediate help.

Customer-facing postmortem summary (concise, non-technical first):
Summary: On 2029-05-29 between 03:12 and 03:47 UTC, a multi-region routing anomaly caused a fast failover that directed some requests to a fallback model variant. Our priority during remediation was to keep customer's latency and availability stable; to do that we accepted a temporary, limited degradation in response fidelity for a small percentage of requests.
Impact: Approximately 0.8% of API calls from a subset of tenants in US-WEST-2 were served by fallback infrastructure or underwent prefix trimming. Most applications saw no visible effect; a small number of customers experienced truncated or less accurate outputs for requests with long context (>3k tokens).
Root cause (short): A control-plane race during capacity rebalancing and an out-of-sync kernel selection rule resulted in fallback routing that did not fully enforce model-variant compatibility checks. This allowed a set of requests to be served by a lower-fidelity variant.
Remediation summary: Engineers corrected the routing policy, tightened compatibility checks, and re-enabled conservative prefix-preservation defaults. We have also added a short-term monitoring alert for abrupt kernel-selection changes and a post-incident test that replays a sampling of long-context requests in staging.

Replay & reconciliation options for customers (actionable choices):
1) Full replay + integrity package (recommended for customers wanting evidence): 
   - What we do: With your consent, we will re-run affected request payloads against the model variant you had pinned (or the closest matching production variant) and produce a signed integrity package containing inputs, outputs (original and replay), timestamps, and a short diff summary.
   - Data retention/TTL: Replays will be attempted for requests retained in our tenant audit logs for up to 30 days post-incident.
   - How to request: Submit a replay request by replying to your incident thread or using the CS portal link (example: /cs/replay-requests/6912). Include tenant id and approximate request timestamps.

2) Sample verification (lighter, faster):
   - What we do: We will select a statistically representative sample of your affected requests (up to 200) and run a reconciliation test. You receive a summary: percent changed, categories of change (truncation, hallucination, tone shift), and example pairs. This is useful if you want a quick sense of scale without reprocessing everything.

3) Opt-out / no action: If your application is tolerant of transient fidelity degradation or you prefer not to request replays, no action is required. We preserve logs for the standard retention period and will include your tenant in any automated regression alerts.

Privacy and compliance notes (short):
- Replays are run only within the same tenant boundary; we do not expose any cross-tenant data.
- Replays may be processed through internal staging infra for deterministic comparison; all infrastructure used adheres to the same encryption and access controls as production.
- If you require HSM/KMS-only processing or air-gapped verification for regulated data, indicate that in the replay request; we will coordinate with your solutions engineer.

Evidence package contents (what customers will receive):
- Request metadata: tenant id, request id(s), original timestamp(s), request size/context length.
- Original output(s) and replay output(s) with model variant labels.
- Small reconciliation summary: token-level change highlights, truncated suffix marker, and a short human-readable note categorizing the change.
- A signed manifest (sig) verifying package integrity.

Customer FAQ snippets (for inclusion in support replies):
Q: Why didn't Redwood just re-run all requests automatically?
A: Automatic replays at scale are risky for some customers (stateful downstream effects, cost, compliance). We require explicit tenant consent so you can choose the scope and processing constraints for replays.

Q: Will request replays change my application data or downstream state?
A: No. Replays are run in read-only inference mode and do not trigger webhooks or state-changing actions. If your application executes side effects based on responses, we will coordinate to avoid duplicate triggers.

Q: How long will it take to get a package?
A: Sample verifications typically complete within 24–72 hours. Full replays depend on volume; we will provide an ETA in the acceptance reply (usually 2–7 business days for typical enterprise volumes).

Operational checklist (internal reminder bullets — include in CS reply as needed):
- [ ] Confirm tenant ownership and authorized contact.
- [ ] Ask for timeframe of suspected impact (start/end).
- [ ] Offer sample verification first for customers unsure of scope.
- [ ] If customer requests full replay, capture processing constraints (KMS/HSM, PII handling, air-gap).
- [ ] Create replay job JIRA and link in reply.

Template escalation note to Solutions/SEs: 
Subject: Replay request from <tenant> for incident 6912 — consent and constraints
Body: quick summary + link to artifact + requested scope + deadline. Tag: eng-applied-ml, eng-serving-runtime, product-hosted-api.

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- Decide whether to expose replay-cost estimate to customers before acceptance. (ops pricing + network/compute).
- Confirm audit log TTL for replay eligibility across legacy accounts.
- Add standard consent checkbox for future incident pages to streamline opt-ins.

Sign-off / contact: 
Priya Desai (Customer Success) — cs@redwood.ai — phone: +1-415-555-0189
Engineering POC: Mark Chen (eng-serving-runtime)

Revision history (internal):
- 2029-06-01: initial draft (Priya)
- 2029-06-04: added evidence package fields and replay constraints (Mark)
- 2029-06-08: clarified sample verification timing and added FAQ (Sofia)

Notes for publishing: Keep the status page snippet separate from the full customer postmortem. Use the status page text for immediate visibility; link to this longer customer postmortem when reaching out via tenant thread or portal.
